Author: Sudhanshu Dhulia
Bench: Sudhanshu Dhulia
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2024
 (Arising out of SLP(Criminal) No.4856/2021)

Sunil Shetty Appell
 Versus
The State Of Maharashtra & Anr. Respon
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The appellant herein is the husband of respondent no.2.
The appellant and respondent no.2 got married on 20.04.2006 and out of the wedlock, they have a daughter, who is presently residing with the wife i.e. respondent no.2.

3. In the year 2018, petition for dissolution of marriage was filed by the appellant bearing Petition No.A-1794 of 2018 before the Family Court at Bandra, Mumbai on the ground of cruelty and harassment.

4. In the year 2019, as a counter blast, the respondent no.2/wife filed an FIR bearing CR No. 49 of 2019 against the appellant and his family members at Chembur Police Station for offences punishable under Section 323,498A,504,506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
5. Reason:
The said proceedings were challenged by the appellant and his family members before the High Court.

After hearing the appellant and his family members of the appellant (Father and his three sisters), the High Court observed that the allegations are vague and generalized in nature as there are no specific allegations of either dowry or torture/harassment.
Consequently, the criminal proceedings against the remaining accused persons such as father and sister of the appellant were dropped.
But the case of the appellant has been kept out and no relief has been granted to the appellant, on ground that there are specific allegations against the husband i.e. the appellant.

sentences.text: We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material placed on record.
We have also gone through the F.I.R. against the appellant as well the allegations that are general in nature and even where these are specific there is no criminal element in the allegations.

The demand of a car pertains to the year 2006, the year when the appellant and respondent no.2 got married and specific allegations on that aspect, if any, also relate to the years after 2006 i.e. 2007,2008 and 2009.

Thereafter, the allegations which are made, reflect nothing but the normal wear and tear of a married life such as the appellant getting angry at the respondent no.2 at car parking, so on and so forth.
We see absolutely no justification that the appellant should face a trial on these allegations.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.

8. The FIR bearing CR No. 49 of 2019 filed against the appellant at Chembur Police Station for offences punishable under Section 323,498A,504,506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and any other proceedings arising out of the said F.I.R. shall stand quashed.
9. We make it clear that if any of the proceedings are pending between the parties, the observations made herein will not prejudiced any of the rights of the parties in those pending cases.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
